transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yeah, thank you for seeing me. So, honestly, what really made me finally make an appointment... because I have been thinking about it for a while, but I just kept putting it off... is work. I am an advertising sales agent, and we have these really, really long strategy meetings. And I mean, they are brutal. We are talking two, sometimes three hours of just sitting in the conference room going over quarterly projections and client pitches. 

And the thing is, I just keep getting up. I know I am supposed to stay seated, like, everyone else is just sitting there with their laptops, totally focused, but I just cannot seem to stay in my chair. I will find literally any excuse. I will get up to refill my water bottle, and the funny thing is I actually bought one of those massive water bottles specifically so I would not need to refill it, but I still do it anyway. Or I will just sort of pace over by the printer, acting like I am waiting for a pitch deck to print out even when I am not. 

It is just so embarrassing because my manager has started giving me these looks, you know, like she is wondering why I am moving around again. I try to tell myself to just sit through it, but then twenty minutes in, I just feel like I need to do something, and before I know it, I am up again. It is just becoming a real issue for my professional image, I think, and I really need to figure out why I cannot just sit through a meeting.
Can you tell me if you find it hard to stay seated or feel restless in other situations, like during meals, while watching a movie, or in social gatherings?

You know, it's actually really weird, but no, not really. Like, if you take movies for example... my boyfriend is a huge movie buff, so we go to the theater all the time. We specifically go to the ones with those big, plush reclining seats—you know the ones I'm talking about, where you push the button on the inside of the armrest and the footrest comes all the way up? We go probably twice a month, at least. And honestly, once I get my popcorn and my drink, I just recline the seat back and I am completely fine. I don't feel the urge to get up at all, not even to go to the lobby or use the restroom or anything. I just sit there for the whole two or three hours, totally relaxed and watching the screen. 

And meals... meals are pretty much the exact same story. When we're at home, we usually eat dinner at our kitchen island, just sitting on these upholstered barstools I ordered online last year. Which, by the way, were a total nightmare to assemble because the screws didn't line up with the holes, but they turned out to be surprisingly comfortable once I finally got them together. We just sit there and eat and talk about our days, and I never really feel like I need to jump up and pace around or find an excuse to leave the table. Even if we go out to a nice restaurant, or if we go to a friend's house for a long sit-down dinner party, I can sit through the whole appetizer, main course, dessert, everything, without doing that weird pacing thing I do at the office. 

It really just seems to be those awful, endless strategy meetings at work where I suddenly just... can't stay in my chair. So yeah, I haven't really noticed that restless feeling outside of the office at all, now that I really stop and think about it. It's just at work.

Can you tell me if you have trouble focusing or staying attentive during tasks or activities outside of these meetings, like when you're reading, working on smaller projects at home, or listening to someone speak?

Well, since you brought up reading... yeah, actually, that is a huge thing for me. Like, outside of those big meetings, I still have to do a ton of reading, especially these massive client briefs. And these briefs, I mean, they are just incredibly dense. Our account managers put them together, and they insist on including absolutely everything, from the client's brand voice guidelines to their target demographic breakdowns, which usually involves all these tiny charts and graphs about household income and media consumption habits that you can barely read anyway. 

So I will sit down at my desk, or even if I bring my laptop home to work on the couch—which I really try not to do because my cat, Barnaby, always tries to sit on the keyboard, but sometimes I just have to catch up—I will tell myself, "Okay, you just need to get through this." And I always start out really focused! I'll have my coffee, I'm sitting up straight, I'm reading the first page, and I feel totally dialed in. 

But then, maybe just a few minutes later, I will suddenly sort of snap out of it and realize I have been staring at the exact same paragraph, or like, the same slide if it's a digital deck, for I don't even know how long. And I will have absolutely no idea what the last point was. It's like my eyes are physically moving over the words, and I'm seeing the letters, but nothing is actually registering in my brain. I'll read a sentence about, I don't know, Q3 digital marketing deliverables, and then I get to the end of the section and realize I was actually thinking about what to make for dinner, or if I remembered to switch the laundry to the dryer before I left the house. 

So then I have to go all the way back up to the top of the page and start completely over, which is just incredibly frustrating because it makes everything take twice as long as it should. It happens in those longer strategy meetings too, honestly. Even if I am managing to stay in my chair, I'll be staring right at the presentation slide, and suddenly I realize the presenter is on a completely different topic and I missed the entire transition. So, yes, staying focused on things like reading those briefs is definitely a struggle for me.
